thread:
Alex Chang: Heads-up — planning a small A/B pricing experiment next Mon to test a new 'per-request priority' surcharge vs a flattened request tier. Need quick alignment on how we treat existing/legacy customers.
Alex Chang: Variant A = current per-token rates + priority fee (0.5 cents/request). Variant B = single per-request tier that bundles priority (price TBD).
Alex Chang: Sheet with cohorts + sample invoices: https://redwood.atlassian.net/sheets/pricing-expt-2026 (editable)
Alex Chang: Questions: 1) Do we keep legacy customers on current rate (no change) or automatically migrate with a temporary credit? 2) Do partners (marketplace vendors) get included in canary? 3) Approval window for marketing email copy.
Maria Gomez: Thanks Alex. Quick clarifying Qs — what's the initial canary size you want? and the rollback criteria? :eyes:
Raj Patel: +1 on Maria. Also need to know whether any enterprise contracts have explicit rate locks in SOWs. If yes we must exempt or apply credits.
Alex Chang: Plan proposal: canary 5% of non-enterprise customers for 48h, then 20% for 7 days if signals okay. Rollback if revenue per-req delta > 30% or >0.5% increase in support tickets.
Alex Chang: For legacy entitlements: suggested behavior = auto-migrate but issue a one-time invoice credit covering delta for first billing cycle (so they see no immediate surprise). After 90 days we move them to new pricing.
Maria Gomez: Legal flagged that some customers have 'rate protection' clauses. We should have an explicit opt-out for enterprise accounts and an opt-in notification for others. Can we add a 'legacy_hold' tag so we don't touch contracts? :memo:
Raj Patel: I'll query contracts and vendor list. If a customer bought via marketplace, we need partner approval; marketplace transactions are governed by partner terms.
billing-bot: Generated preview CSV: /mnt/exports/pricing-expt-2015678901-preview.csv (1.8k rows)
billing-bot: Top 10 impacted customers by spend included in the CSV.
Alex Chang: Marketplace vendors: exclude from initial canary. Good call, Raj. We'll only include direct-pay self-serve customers for 5% canary.
Maria Gomez: Timeline check — need marketing/legal signoff by Fri EOD to hit Mon. I can prepare the email draft today. Who owns the wording?
Alex Chang: I'll draft copy for the experiment cohort (short note + opt-out link). Maria — can you route to legal once you have the draft? Raj — can you confirm contract exemptions by Thurs?
Raj Patel: On it. I'll push a query tomorrow and DM with any hard exemptions. Also I can draft the invoice-credit calc: credit = max(0, old_total - new_total) for first statement, plus note.
Maria Gomez: OK approved for canary: 5% for 48h, email copy to be reviewed. :white_check_mark:
Alex Chang: Awesome — putting a holdback in the rollout plan: tag = expt_priority_apr2026, canary_pct=5, duration=48h, grace_credit=true
Alex Chang: rollout snippet for ops (for eng-platform):
```
experiment:
  id: expt_priority_apr2026
  cohorts:
    - name: canary
      pct: 5
      duration: 48h
    - name: ramp
      pct: 20
      duration: 7d
  legacy_policy: auto_migrate_with_one_time_credit(90d)
  include_marketplace: false
```
Raj Patel: I'll prepare a short vendor note for partners in Marketplace to reassure them. Will coordinate with partner-ops.
Maria Gomez: Thanks team. If any blockers pop up, @alex_chang please escalate. Otherwise I'll send draft to legal in ~2h and loop everyone for sign-off.
Alex Chang: Thanks — will ping when prod flags are ready. :rocket:
